# CoApi

> Zero-boilerplate auto-configuration for Spring HTTP Interface (@HttpExchange) clients on Spring Boot 4.x / Spring Framework 7.x. Annotate an interface with @CoApi and inject it; CoApi backs it with WebClient (reactive) or RestClient (sync), with optional Spring Cloud LoadBalancer support.

Published docs: https://coapi.ahoo.me (Chinese: https://coapi.ahoo.me/zh/). Agent guidance for this repository: AGENTS.md.

## Getting Started

- [What is CoApi?](wiki/getting-started/overview.md): purpose, capabilities, when to use it, version compatibility
- [Installation](wiki/getting-started/installation.md): starter, required WebClient/RestClient builder starter, optional load balancer and java-jwt, artifacts
- [Quick Start](wiki/getting-started/quick-start.md): define, configure and inject a reactive or sync client

## Guide

- [Defining Clients](wiki/deep-dive/annotations.md): @CoApi attributes, base URL resolution, @LoadBalanced, naming, URI-per-request clients, shared contracts
- [Registering Clients](wiki/deep-dive/auto-configuration.md): classpath scanning, coapi.base-packages, @EnableCoApi, CoApiDefinition beans, use without Spring Boot
- [Client Modes](wiki/deep-dive/client-modes.md): REACTIVE / SYNC / AUTO, return types, builder beans
- [Load Balancing](wiki/deep-dive/load-balancing.md): serviceId, lb://, Spring Cloud LoadBalancer wiring, per-environment overrides
- [Customization](wiki/deep-dive/customization.md): per-client filters/interceptors, builder customizers, replacing beans
- [Authentication](wiki/deep-dive/authentication.md): HeaderSetFilter, BearerTokenFilter, CachedExpirableTokenProvider
- [Examples](wiki/deep-dive/examples.md): the runnable example modules

- [Architecture](wiki/deep-dive/architecture.md): internals, design rules, where to change what
